In the South London Schools championship for Intermediates, Adrian Major representing Tulse Hill School became the fourth Belgrave holder of the title in six years.

Bradshaw was third on stage 1 behind both Mitcham 'A' and 'B' teams, but Keys soon split his opponents on the second leg and Hayes ran us to a safe second at the last change-over. Although he had no hope of catching the winners Adrian Major still turned in fastest time of our quartet.
Adrian Major, however, finished only 17 secs. behind and pushed Hayes back into third place. This trio of youngsters show every promis of keeping Belgrave's name to the fore in years to come.

Unfortunately, Adrian Major was not at his best and we were well down after stage 1. Ron Hayes made ground with a good run on stage two and John Bicourt, with 3rd fastest time of the day, took us up to 6th and within striking distance of 4th.

In the Youths, Adrian Major, Ron Hayes, Bill Bruce and more recently Derek Hurd have shown considerable potential and if they maintain their progress they could well be strengthening the senior ranks in a few years time.

Ron Hayes ran his best race to date to finish 9th with Adrian Major only one place behind. Despite the forward running of our first three, Walton pipped us for 2nd place by 4 points, thus reducing our final margin to 12 points.
Adrian Major also had a fine run to finish 10th and was ably supported by Ron Hayes (19th) and Derek Hurd (27th) to give us a comfortable 3rd place.
John was well backed up by Adrian Major, 39th,Derek Hurd 54th, and Ron Hayes 75th - the team did wel[illegible] to take 6th place with 186 points.

Hand over fist he closed on the quartet scrambling up to the finish and just managed to split them in two a few yards from the line---another 30yards would have seen him an easy 5th. Adrian Major had a good run to finish 62nd and Ron Hayes produced his usual sound performance to be our 3rd man.

John Bicourt, the only youth in the first six, did very well to lead the rest of the field home, and showed promise of great things in the "Southern" and "National". Adrian Major was the 2nd youth home (7th) and is fast joining the "elite".

Adrian Major set off, knowing that he was unlikely to make any impression on Badgery of Mitcham, but determined to hold on to 2nd place. This he did easily and was 7th fastest man in the overall classification.

The youths section is definitely the strongest it has ever been,with a whole host of budding stars.Performances by J.Vivian,A.Major and John Martin, ably supported by many others,overshadow some of our seniors' efforts.
Back again to the winter,Adrian Major has had a very good season and it is most noticeable that in this section a potential star emerges each year.

A great run by Adrian Major in this opening fixture. Church and Badgery have already made names for themselves in the Youth athletics world and it is certain that Adrian is on the brink of making his also.

Absolutely no trouble for Adrian Major who cleared out right from the start. However,the fight for the minor positions was a different matter, with the result still in the balance until the last few yards.

Just before the start of the second lap Adrian Major shot past Dave Cocks and within 100yds had opened up a 50yd gap. Jack,by this time,had dropped back somewhat,but had no difficulty in holding his 4th place.
Adrian "Galloping" Major ran next and set about the field in no mean fashion taking us through to 3rd and recording one of the fastest times of the day.

The most impressive runs were by Adrian Major, a youth, and by Jack Brown, almost a veteran. Adrian's relentless pace took him thro' to sixth-fastest time of the day, whilst Jack showed a fine turn of speed to hold off scratch men Black and Hart.

Other juniors who have had a good season are John Mitchell,John Martin, Phil Smith,Bob Nelson,Dave Nicklin and Adrian Major. Many others who are under the guidance of Tom Carter are improving fast and the seniors will surely benefit in the very near future.
Adrian Major contributed a great deal with his individual placings of 3,3,6,5, and our young team will have to work hard next season to compensate for his loss to the Senior/Junior league.

Adrian Major was a little disappointed to fall one place short of his 62nd position of last year. However, he is a greatly improved runner and we should see great things when he joins John Bicourt in the Junior ranks next year.
Although Adrian Major only finished 7th in the mile he recorded a personal best of 4:29.4 - not bad this early in the season.

Adrian Major ran well in the 2 miles to record a personal best of 9:38.2 . Badgery and Church,as expected,tore off into the lead,but Adrian ran a steadier race working his way through the field until just after the half-way mark he went into 3rd place which he held to the finish.

Perhaps the unluckiest athlete of the evening was Dave Nicklin who was doomed to finish second to Denis in each race. John Martin,better known for his shot-putting activities, nearly caused an upset by almost catching Adrian Major on the tape in the 'half'.

John Kelly put up the fastest time in the heats of the youths 880y (2:07.0) but couldn't quite repeat the performance in the final (2:10.0), a good performance nevertheless. Other Belgrave members to do well were Dave Nicklin 3rd in the Long Jump (20'1½") and Adrian Major 4th in the Mile(4:35.2 [?]).
In the Junior events,Adrian Major found the 880/mile double too much for him - he won the mile in 4:47.0 but was beaten in the half by Richard Moody who recorded 2:07.3 .

Adrian Major and Chris Steer both made up two places but by this time the first two clubs (Windsor and Reading) were well ahead and it was left to John Bicourt and Mel Thorpe to maintain 3rd position, although Mel was closing fast on Reading towards the end.
Adrian Major was 50 yards clear of the field at one point but had to give way to the experienced'Valley'men, eventually finishing a good 5th, backed up closely in 7th place, by Bob Glover.

Chris Steer's effort was particularly good - he improves every time out. D.Brew and R.James indicated we shall be seeing quite a lot more of them - the latter winning the handicap jointly with Adrian Major.

Not far behind the "flying" Thorpe was young Adrian Major, whose run was no less noteworthy. For a first year junior to finish as high as 12th in this field of mainly senior runners, and only 22 seconds behind the winner, was an effort of which he can feel truly proud.
John Bicourt and Adrian Major are, of course, far and away the leading pair but we have a good prospect in new member Michael Baker from Battersea College of Technology.
Meanwhile, Adrian Major was having a battle royal with the rest of Mitcham's scoring team and after running one of his best races to date,he finished a very distinguished 5th.

This was a good day for Tom Carter's 'school', with Tony Fairclough taking the Senior '10' by 1 second and Adrian Major winning the Junior '5' by what must be the largest margin ever - 5 minutes 11 seconds!
Adrian Major, of whom we expected a good performance was left behind and had the invidious task of chasing the field whereas he would normaly have been contesting the lead.

The loss this season of Adrian Major to the Senior/Junior league hit any hopes we might have had of improving on last year's 3rd place. Once again Mitcham and Croydon took first two places whilst Hercules jumped from their bottom place of last year into third position.
Team mate Adrian Major ran to form, making enough ground on the final lap to pass John a mile from home, but his lack of a finish enabled Bicourt to re-pass him 200 yards out.

Geoff North was second fastest of the day, ahead of Strong,Tulloh and Wiggs, and Adrian Major proved himself capable of holding his own in any of our first teams by turning in a notable sub-17 minute run.

Chris and young Adrian Major looked in fine fettle but Laurie O'Hara was showing the effects of recent 'flu'.
